messages:
sasha: heads up — overnight scrub in us-west2 flagged ext4 metadata errors on a few gnodes. some mounts switched to readonly and GPU provisioning is failing for pods. i'm attaching snippets below. @ops-oncall please take a look.

infra-bot: alert: scrub-job-usw2 finished with 9 warnings across gnode pool (see: https://internal/alerts/alert-493876) :warning:

aj: which hostnames specifically? is scrub overlapping with fstrim or other disk jobs?

sasha: gnode-73, gnode-128, gnode-274. fstrim cron at 01:08, scrub kicked at 01:15 — looks like an overlap window.

maya: i've got one of those nodes in my test cluster — here's the dmesg tail from gnode-73:
```
[Jan 28 01:16:22] EXT4-fs warning (device nvme0n1p1): ext4_end_bio:322: I/O error -5 writing to inode 84723 (offset 0x0, size 0x2000)
[Jan 28 01:16:22] EXT4-fs (nvme0n1p1): Remounting filesystem read-only
[Jan 28 01:16:23] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345
```

liam: autoscaler logs show this when trying to create pods: `Failed to attach volumes: rpc error: code = Internal desc = device is read-only` — so sched is refusing disks.

aj: NVMe SMART looks noisy on gnode-128, quick output: 
```
$ smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1
SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: FAILED
Media_Error_Count: 45
Error Information Log Entries: 102
```

ops-oncall: @sasha taking ownership. i'll cordon affected nodes and start reprovision for non-prod ones. can someone list current pods stuck in Pending?

sasha: small list attached (pods: gpu-trainer-12, batch-job-9). i'll move noncritical workloads off gnode-73.

maya: mitigation idea: pause scrub for the suspect pool and stagger fstrim -> scrub by 30m to avoid simultaneous heavy IO. also lower concurrent-scrub-workers from 4 -> 1 as a throttle.

aj: agree. i'll draft a quick runbook: 1) pause scrub on suspect nodes 2) cordon + reprovision 3) run nvme fw check + SMART scrub 4) optionally offload GPUs to dedicated pool.

liam: quick question — is this likely wear-leveling hitting a threshold (heatmap) or an overlayfs/fstrim interaction?

maya: initial theory: scrub + fstrim concurrently causing heavy small-block IO and exposing flaky media sectors; wear seems elevated but health counters point to read/write retries. firmware bug still possible.

ops-oncall: cordon started for gnode-73 and 128. reprovisioning gnode-73 now (non-prod). will keep gnode-274 in rotation until we confirm reprovision outcome. ETA ~15m.

sasha: can we add a short-term routing rule to avoid scheduling new GPU jobs to the entire us-west2 scrub pool? saves slowness while we investigate.

aj: will add a node-affinity deny rule for scrub-pool via k8s label selector. also will open an infra ticket for firmware check and janitor scrub schedule change.

maya: for followup — capture `nvme error-log` and `dmesg` on reprovisioned hosts and attach to the ticket. i'll run a light read-only scrub (no write) once reprovision done.

liam: :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: reprovision finished for gnode-73, mount remounted rw, running nvme health checks now. will report back in 10m.

sasha: thanks all. i'll hold off on any large batch launches to us-west2 until we have green from ops-oncall.

infra-bot: incident-note: us-west2 scrub-readonly ripple — nodes cordoned: gnode-73,gnode-128; reprovision in progress; followup ticket INFRA-8421 created.

aj: FYI i'll schedule a scrub-stagger change for next maintenance window and add telemetry to detect scrub+fstrim overlap automatically.

maya: noted — will help with log parsing rule.

ops-oncall: update: nvme error-log on gnode-73 shows repeated LBA retries, but firmware version matches fleet baseline. moving gnode-73 to replacement pool pending SMART repair.

sasha: ok, closing slack here for now, continue updates in INFRA-8421. thanks.
